raw.query: WITH head AS (SELECT (metrics->>'total_images')::numeric / (metrics->>'requests')::numeric AS head_img_per_req FROM provenance.encoder_run_summary WHERE run_id = 'sweeps:vision_head2k_s1'), trace AS (SELECT value_num AS trace_img_per_req FROM provenance.eda_metric WHERE metric_path = 'numimages.mean_images_per_request_overall'), steady AS (SELECT mean_img_per_s / mean_req_per_s AS steady_img_per_req FROM provenance.windows WHERE window_name = 'steady24h') SELECT ROUND(head_img_per_req, 3) AS head_img_per_req, ROUND(trace_img_per_req::numeric, 3) AS trace_img_per_req, ROUND(steady_img_per_req::numeric, 3) AS steady_img_per_req FROM head, trace, steady;
raw.observed: head: 2.879 img/req, trace: 14.332 img/req, steady24h: 5.326 img/req
raw.claimed: head: 2.9 img/req, trace: ≈14 img/req, steady24h corrects this
raw.evidence: The 24-hour steady window (steady24h) has only 5.326 images per request, which remains highly vision-lean and fails to correct the 2.9 value back to the full trace average of 14.332.
raw.fix: Revise the claim to state that the 24-hour steady window remains highly vision-lean (at 5.3 images per request, or ~37% of the trace average) rather than asserting it corrects the vision-lean property of the steady head.
